findings: The 2026-11-07 base capture is a variant directory for Checkout, Elements with Checkout Sessions or Payment Intents, Direct API and mobile iOS, Android and React Native (new raw 5–21). The paired 2026-05-07 capture includes bodies for all seven variants (old raw 8–2513). All seven new links correspond to historically documented paths. The capture shape and Markdown target URLs change, but the linked bodies were not read as November authority.

The diff is an export comparison. Its line 2514 joins the prior final line with the new Checkout addition, and the hunk does not represent the raw capture metadata. The separately read pinned raws verify each side (old raw 1–6, 2509–2513 and new raw 1–13).

The dated Checkout body explicitly requires MX business location, MXN, payment mode and single-currency one-time line items, with manual `oxxo` listing distinct from dynamic payment methods (old raw 12–50, 241–275). The generated store-cash voucher and Checkout form completion precede eventual async success or failure (old raw 172–194).

The existing source retains historical Checkout, expiry and `hosted_voucher_url` information (source 13–21), but Direct API billing details and deprecation wording conflict with the May capture, mobile scope is incomplete, and `fill_never` conflates voucher expiry and failure notification (source 13–27).
historical_claims_to_preserve: Use the 2026-05-07 capture date from old raw line 2 even though the filename says 2025. Keep its raw citation and date the fully documented variant behavior. Checkout and Elements with Checkout Sessions retain the documented MX/MXN one-time Checkout constraints (old raw 18–50, 233–275), the valid email and Account/Customer parameter distinction in Checkout Elements (475–527), and the Session/client-secret identity distinct from the separately server-created MXN PaymentIntent and its client secret in Payment Intents Elements (958–1088).

Preserve the Checkout voucher redirect and Checkout Session events with the related PaymentIntent outcome (old raw 172–194). Mobile and Direct API use PaymentIntent confirmation to create or show the voucher, with the customer paying cash separately and success determined asynchronously. The iOS `.succeeded` and Android `PaymentResult.Completed` client callbacks in those examples signify voucher display (old raw 1429–1462, 1668–1720). React Native displays a voucher webview and treats `RequiresAction` as voucher creation while awaiting payment (old raw 1922–2004). The May mobile/Direct guides describe next-business-day notification for paid vouchers, excluding Mexican holidays, with funds unavailable immediately (old raw 1474–1487, 2016–2029, 2294–2307).

Keep historic `expires_after_days` as the optional 1–7 calendar-day option, default 3, with the cited 23:59 America/Mexico_City cutoff and separate `next_action.oxxo_display_details.expires_after` timestamp (old raw 105–107, 2191–2193, 2383–2407). Separate voucher expiration from the post-expiry processing/failure window and retry/cancel state. Mobile and Direct API say a voucher cannot be cancelled before expiry (old raw 1474–1487, 1529–1533, 2294–2307, 2509–2513).

The May Direct API path is supported Legacy and no longer recommended, with possible future deprecation. Its form needs full name and email; the client calls `stripe.confirmOxxoPayment()` using the server-created PaymentIntent's client secret (old raw 2077–2103, 2195–2278). Sandbox test cases and package versions are dated and variant-specific (old raw 350–381, 1294–1304, 1562–1583, 2323–2347).
conflicts: Source line 23 and voucher concept line 107 say email alone is required for the legacy web Direct API. The May Direct API instructions explicitly require both full name and email, with a two-character minimum for each of first and last name, and the form and client call pass both (old raw 2195–2221, 2244–2264). Correct the source and the reciprocal `stripe-vouchers.md` integration statement.

Source lines 13 and 27 say the Legacy section is marked deprecated. The May block identifies the Direct API path as supported but no longer recommended and says support might end if it is deprecated (old raw 2077–2083). The November link at line 17 supplies no new deprecation status.

Source lines 13 and 17 characterize mobile coverage as iOS and Android only. The May guide has a material React Native body (old raw 1793–2075), and November still lists it (new raw 18–21). The voucher concept's May integration list at line 107 likewise misses React Native. The source line 17 comparative superlative about breadth across voucher methods has no support in the paired captures.

Source line 25 presents 1 business day plus 2 calendar days as the `fill_never` voucher expiry duration, while old raw lines 218–220 and 2345–2347 attach the interval to failure webhook arrival in that test row. The historical general expiry cutoff is independently defined at old raw lines 105–107 and 2191–2193.

The May historical expiry sections use abbreviated wording about `requires_payment_method` after expiration (old raw 1529–1533, 2509–2513), while their full event sections describe a `processing` interval when an expired voucher can no longer be paid and a later payment failure or success (old raw 1474–1487, 2294–2307). Preserve the state boundary and avoid implying immediate retry/cancel at the cutoff or universal event timing from the test row.

findings: Retain May 7, 2026 provenance and route the November 7 base capture as a navigation reference, with the complete May React Native variant alongside iOS and Android (old raw 1793–2075 and new raw 18–21). Clarify the fulfillment boundary in the source's current Checkout event shorthand (source 19; old raw 184–194).

The voucher concept at lines 95–109 and source route at line 123 resolve the main topic through the Stripe index at lines 372–383. The concept's own line 107 repeats the email-only error and omits May React Native coverage.
conflicts: Direct API requires full name and email (source 23 versus old raw 2195–2221); the May guide labels this supported Legacy path no longer recommended with deprecation conditional (source 13 and 27 versus old raw 2077–2083).

The documented `fill_never` interval describes failure webhook arrival (source 25 versus old raw 218–220, 2345–2347). The May guide documents React Native and the source's claimed breadth relative to other voucher methods lacks evidence (source 13, 17 versus old raw 1793–2075 and new raw 18–21).
source_assessments.reason: The November raw change is navigation only. Independently, current-source billing prerequisites, support labeling and failure-event semantics can mislead implementation decisions. The existing mobile list also omits a whole documented May variant.

answers.Q1: The 2026-11-07 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/oxxo/accept-a-payment identifies OXXO as a Mexican payment method and routes Checkout, Elements with the Checkout Sessions or Payment Intents API, Direct API, and iOS, Android and React Native (new raw lines 5-21). The base index establishes those routes only. The 2026-05-07 capture documents in-store cash payment with a generated voucher, and for Checkout an MX business, MXN, payment mode and one-time line items (old raw lines 12-50). Checkout Session submission generates a voucher and later async success is the fulfillment signal (old raw lines 172-194). Elements with Checkout Sessions hands a server-created Session client secret to the client, while Payment Intents Elements uses the server-created PaymentIntent and its client secret (old raw lines 271-305 and old raw lines 958-1088). Direct API and mobile confirmation can issue or display the voucher while payment awaits the customer, and the server observes the later PaymentIntent outcome (old raw lines 1950-2029 and old raw lines 2195-2307). source-stripe-oxxo-accept-payment.md retains historical Checkout and expiry details but misses React Native and misstates Direct API billing details, Legacy status and the `fill_never` interval.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/oxxo/accept-a-payment, the switch from detailed bodies to seven Markdown variant links is presentational and navigational (new raw lines 9-21). May already included React Native (old raw lines 1793-1805 and old raw lines 1922-2004). The base index provides no substantive product/API change, no renewed version or eligibility evidence, and no confirmation of linked variant bodies. source-stripe-oxxo-accept-payment.md should keep the 2026-05-07 detail and May-specific qualifications: Checkout Session completion creates a payable voucher, while Checkout async success corresponds to `PaymentIntent.succeeded` (old raw lines 172-194). On mobile and Direct API, client confirmation or voucher display precedes later server-side paid/failed events, and the May expiry cutoff is distinct from post-expiry `processing` and failure (old raw lines 1429-1487 and old raw lines 2294-2307). Keep the 1–7 day voucher option, default 3, and distinct `expires_after` timestamp dated (old raw lines 2191-2193 and old raw lines 2396-2407). Correct the source and its voucher concept where they say Direct API requires only email; May requires full name and email (old raw lines 2195-2221). Describe Direct API as May's supported but discouraged Legacy route with deprecation conditional (old raw lines 2077-2083), and identify `fill_never` as a failure-webhook arrival interval from the test table (old raw lines 2323-2347). None of these snapshots establishes a successful transaction, account eligibility or settlement.
